newsitem.title: USA: AT&T, Hewlett in electronic commerce pact.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Hewlett in electronic commerce pact.

text.p: AT&T Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co said they agreed to a multi-phase alliance designed to make it easier for companies to conduct business over the Internet, via electronic storefronts and intranets.

In a joint statement issued Monday, the two companies said the pact would focus on developing products to make merchant use of electronic commerce easier via outsourced electronic communications and commerce services.
AT&T will provide networking and secure-purchasing capabilities and H-P will provide enterprise computing and reliability systems, they said.

AT&T said it plans to recruit H-P's nearly 15,000 resellers to join AT&T's Marketing Alliance Program as agents to sell AT&T's Web site services, such as Web hosting, which provides companies with Web sites situated on AT&T computers.

AT&T and H-P said they will integrate their technologies to create electronic storefront systems that will allow merchants to host Web sites capable of secure electronic transactions. Such electronic commerce systems will be built around AT&T's SecureBuy Service, which provides infrastructure and management.
The partners said they would collaborate with iCat Corp. and other electronic commerce software developers to help merchants process orders and serve customers.
The alliance will also build on AT&T's existing relationship with Open Market Inc in which AT&T has integrated Open Market's electronic commerce software into its SecureBuy system.

It was not evident from the statement what role H-P's Verifone unit would play in the alliance. Verifone is a leading supplier of electronic commerce systems. Hewlett closed the $1.29 billion acquisition of Verifone in late June.
A Hewlett-Packard spokesman was not immediately available to comment. The companies scheduled a conference call to discuss the deal at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
AT&T and H-P said they will bring together their current electronic commerce, network services, hardware, software, consulting and support to deliver additional new products and services.
AT&T Labs and H-P Labs will collaborate to develop new technologies to improve the reliability and continuous availability of Internet-based network services.
The teams will look at ways to assure consistent high-quality network performance.
Hewlett was up 2-3/16 at 63-3/8 by late morning Monday, an all-time high for the stock. AT&T stood at 35-1/4, even on the day.
